newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iberia to up ex-France cargo rates July 1.
newsitem.headline: Iberia to up ex-France cargo rates July 1.

text.p: Spanish state airline Iberia said it will increase its ex-France cargo rates to selected destinations by an average of five percent, effective July 1.
"In April 1997, we raised ex-France rates to several destinations in southern Latin America, notably Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Chile," a Paris-based Iberia cargo official told Reuters.
"The next round of increases will include Central America and northern Latin America, with Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador among the countries concerned," he added.
Iberia said it last raised its ex-France rates on these routes in July 1996.
The increases will also extend to the U.S. (New York and Miami) and Europe, the official said.

Iberia operates several flights daily from Paris to Madrid using Airbus 300 and 320 passenger aircraft and also serves several other Spanish cities from the French capital, including Barcelona, Seville, Valencia and Zaragosa.
The airline also trucks freight between France and Spain.
